page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Deep Learning Boost (AVX512_VNNI). The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.g7.2xlarge consistently in the average performance tier. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng yield scores of 1841.19 and 7764.36 respectively, while Geekbench multi-core performance reaches 6005.0. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by a read-only small block bandwidth of 426.28 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 39.31 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates solid capabilities in specialized tasks, achieving 7.99 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 12.01 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

While the instance handles lightweight machine learning tasks well—processing 753.54 tokens per second for a small 135M parameter LLM—it exhibits significant performance degradation on larger models, dropping to 7.66 tokens per second for text generation with a 7B parameter model. This highlights a clear tradeoff: the lack of a dedicated GPU and the general-purpose CPU allocation make it unsuitable for heavy AI inference or training. However, its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and dedicated CPU allocation make it highly cost-efficient for standard enterprise workloads. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose business applications.
